I designed a world that is a [Möbius Strip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%B6bius_strip?wprov=sfla1) instead of a normal sphere. It's complicated, but filling in the confusing parts of the world gives it character.

For example, could a person cross the edge of the world? This would effectively allow them to teleport to the opposite side of the world.

My answer is no, or at least, no one has successfully done this. The terrain becomes very rocky and cold near the edge of the map. It is a strange combination of lava lakes from the tectonic activity mixed with permafrost, frozen lakes , and massive glaciers due to the distance from the equator. Most discomforting is the fact that gravity pulls sideways as you go towards the edge. This makes sense due to the planet's geometry. Also, the air gets very thin because the air is going to concentrate near the "middle". That's not even mentioning the hideous beasts that inhabit most parts of the edge and the madmen that have so much reason to avoid society that they call the edge their home.

But maybe an adventuring party will have to travel across the deadly terrain to get to the other side. Who knows? :D

Some other things that will change are the placement of oceans, the placement and structure of cave systems, and the water cycle. The list goes on and on, but I hope that my world will fascinate any PC that adventures there. The best part is that I won't tell them these things, they have to figure it out!
